title: BAGMAN Source
description: Canonical `Source` (PID §9). Describes where information originated. Provider-specific identity belongs underneath the source model (via `provider` / `external_source_ref`), never as canonical BAGMAN identity.

source_id.description: Canonical BAGMAN identifier for this source.

source_type.description: The kind of source. Deliberately open (NOT a closed enum), for the same extensibility reason as `GovernedEntity.entity_type` (PID §4/§9). Known initial values (documentation only, not an enforced closed set): `MAILBOX`, `MANUAL_UPLOAD`, `BANK`, `ACCOUNTING_PLATFORM`, `BILLING_PLATFORM`, `GENERATED`, `API`. `MANUAL_UPLOAD` is included from CD-2 so a future upload GUI (PID §26) requires no schema change.

provider.description: The concrete provider/system behind this source. Deliberately open (not a closed enum) — new providers must be addable without schema redesign. Known initial example values (documentation only): `MICROSOFT_GRAPH`, `IMAP`, `GMAIL`, `STARLING`, `REVOLUT`, `XERO`, `CHARGEBEE`, `USECURE`, `HUNTRESS`, `INTERNAL`.

external_source_ref.description: An optional provider-scoped identity string for this source, e.g. a mailbox address such as `matt@infosecurs.com`. This is NOT a secret — it is an identity string only (never a credential, password, or token; see PID §29).

governed_entity_hint.description: An optional hint referencing a `GovernedEntity` by `canonical_name` or `entity_id`. This is explicitly a HINT, not an ownership assertion: per PID §9, "a source may provide an entity hint without asserting canonical ownership." For example, a mailbox provider hint of `matt@infosecurs.com` does not mean all records observed from that mailbox automatically belong to Infosecurs. `null` means no hint is available.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the source. Deliberately open (not a closed enum).

metadata.description: Free-form, genuinely open metadata about the source. Must not contain secrets or credentials (PID §29).
